criterion: Acceptance: live row, Claude pane in default and auto mode with the rule in its settings
finding: The default-mode and auto-mode rows prove the rule through --allowedTools, not a settings entry
why: The contract bullet requires the rule in the pane's settings, and the spawn check and the H15 offer both work on settings files, so the row does not prove the path they serve.
fix: Re-run both panes with Bash(afk-team *) in a settings file the pane reads (user or project), or record the settings-file case as unverified in the row.
evidence: "The rule reached them only through `--allowedTools 'Bash(afk-team *)'`, which stands in for the settings entry: no settings file was written." vs Acceptance "with the rule in its settings, runs `afk-team agent-list '{}'` with no prompt"

finding: Three launcher-refusal tests build PATH from the host PATH, so a host with the real afk-bin on PATH (the state /afk:setup creates) makes them fail.
why: check_afk_team_launcher runs `command -v afk-team` in a shell that inherits the host PATH tail; once the host afk-bin holds afk-team, the found file is the real launcher and the message becomes `afk-team on PATH is ..., not the launcher ...`, not the asserted `is missing` / `is not on PATH`.
fix: Build the child PATH from the bash directory plus the tmp afk-bin only, or add a tmp afk-bin-free PATH, so no host afk-team can resolve.
evidence: test_a_missing_launcher_refuses: `home["paths"]["team"].unlink()` then asserts `the afk-team launcher ... is missing`; test_a_launcher_off_path_refuses: `home["env"]["PATH"] = home["env"]["PATH"].split(os.pathsep, 1)[1]`; test_a_wiped_afk_bin_refuses_naming_setup: `shutil.rmtree(home["paths"]["bin"])`; fixture: `env["PATH"] = os.pathsep.join([str(paths["bin"]), env.get("PATH", "")])`. Inferred (not run): this host's PATH already holds C:/Users/mvu/AppData/Local/afk/python/afk-bin (command -v afk-python resolves there) and has no afk-team yet.

finding: One afk-bin launcher serves two harness plugin copies, so a setup run from the other harness repoints it and the Claude check then refuses `launcher`
why: PROVIDERS.md:28 gives each harness its own managed plugin directory (`~/.claude/plugins` vs `~/.codex/plugins`), but afk-bin is per user and `place_team_launcher` rewrites whenever bytes differ, so the last harness to run setup wins; inferred (not run with both harnesses installed).
fix: Decide the dual-harness case: name it in ADR-0017/MANIFEST H15 Notes, or make check 3 accept a launcher naming any installed copy of this plugin, and stop MANIFEST.md:404 advising a setup run from the other harness without saying it repoints the launcher.
evidence: `def place_team_launcher(paths, windows, root: Path = PLUGIN_ROOT)` writes when `target.read_bytes() != data`; MANIFEST.md:404 "run `/afk:setup` from the other harness to check its rule"; PROVIDERS.md:28 "Managed plugin directory | `~/.claude/plugins` ... | `~/.codex/plugins`"

finding: Possible payload-quoting break: the Windows call path changes from afk-python.exe to afk-team.cmd, and no test or live row sends a payload that holds double quotes.
why: The entry script takes one JSON argument (scripts/afk-team.py:34-38); a batch file passes %* on raw, and PowerShell can drop embedded quotes for a .cmd, so agent-send JSON may arrive as invalid JSON (inferred, unverified: not run here).
fix: Add a live Codex-on-Windows row that sends a payload such as {"agent_id":"a1"} through afk-team.cmd; if it fails, pass the payload another way (file path or escaped form) and say so in the launch prompt.
evidence:
python_runtime.py:312 `files[Path(paths["team_cmd"])] = f'@"{entry}" "{script}" %*
'`; providers/CONFORMANCE.md (diff line 186) Q56 row runs only `afk-team agent-list '{}'`; before this slice the same agent called afk-python.exe with JSON directly (CONFORMANCE.md:511).

criterion: Acceptance: live row, /afk:setup in auto mode writes the launcher (Q55)
finding: The Q55 row ran a driver on a scratch LOCALAPPDATA, not /afk:setup against the real afk-bin
why: An auto-mode classifier can judge a write into the real data folder or the PATH step differently, so the row shows less than the contract names.
fix: State in the row that the real afk-bin write and the PATH step are unverified, or run /afk:setup in an auto-mode pane once.
evidence: "through a driver that dropped the PATH step" and "The real `/afk:setup` adds the PATH step, which this row did not run"

criterion: Acceptance: H15 offer and Probe describe the 3-part check
finding: H15 Probe still defines exit 0 as rule present and no block entry; the launcher condition and the launcher Fix path are not stated
why: Exit 0 now also needs the launcher checks, and a probe answering `launcher` with the rule already present would lead the Fix step to print a rule the human already holds.
fix: Add the launcher condition to the exit-0 sentence, and say a `launcher` answer skips the print-and-wait Fix and routes to P1.
evidence: "exit 0 when this session's harness needs no rule, or when the rule is in an allow list and no block-list entry matches a verb command"

criterion: blast radius: new caller of a changed public symbol
finding: permission.py becomes a second reader of python_runtime.layout()["team"] and team_launcher_root(), but no registry row or docstring names this caller.
why: INV-085 counted setup_secrets.py:45 as the one non-test reader of layout(); a later layout or launcher-format change in python_runtime.py has no pointer to permission.py, so the check would break silently.
fix: Name scripts/team/permission.py as a reader in the python_runtime.py docstring or the FRESHNESS.md python_runtime row.
evidence: permission.py:33 `RUNTIME = PLUGIN / "skills" / "afk" / "setup" / "scripts" / "python_runtime.py"`; :139 `runtime.layout(child, os.name == "nt")["team"]`; INV-085 REPORT: "setup_secrets.py:45 is the one non-test reader of `layout()[\"launcher\"]`"; FRESHNESS.md row for python_runtime.py names no team reader.

finding: Possible install failure on Windows when afk-team or afk-team.cmd is in use: place_team_launcher moves with a bare os.replace, where place_entry renames a locked file away (inferred; not run).
why: A setup run during a live team run, after a plugin update changed the bytes, could hit PermissionError, fail the afk-team step and leave the stamp deleted (install deletes it first); INV-085 lists cmd.exe locking of a running afk-team.cmd as a frontier item.
fix: Either rename the locked file away as place_entry does at :291-297, or record the gap as an accepted limit in MANIFEST P1.
evidence: python_runtime.py:348 `os.replace(staged, target)` inside place_team_launcher with no PermissionError branch; place_entry :291-297 has `except PermissionError:` rename to `.old`; INV-085 Frontier: "cmd.exe locking of a running afk-team.cmd".

finding: No test reaches two of the three failure branches of team_launcher_problem: `is not executable` and `differs from the launcher setup writes`.
why: The `differs` branch is the case of a launcher naming the right plugin folder but a stale afk-python path, and the executable branch guards the POSIX bit that place_team_launcher rewrites; both could break unseen.
fix: Add a check test with right-root but different bytes, and a POSIX-only test with matching bytes and mode 0o644 that expects a rewrite and a failing check.
evidence: `return None if windows or os.access(target, os.X_OK) else f"{target} is not executable"` and `return f"{target} differs from the launcher setup writes"`; tests cover only `launcher missing` and `names the plugin folder`.

finding: check_afk_team_launcher's `names no plugin folder`, `no POSIX shell`, `afk-bin cannot be located` and shell-timeout branches have no test.
why: Each is a refusal path that must name /afk:setup; an unreadable or hand-edited launcher is the likely real-world case for the first.
fix: Add one test writing garbage into the tmp afk-team and asserting a launcher refusal containing `names no plugin folder`; inject `run` to cover the timeout.
evidence: `if named is None: return f"the launcher {want} names no plugin folder"`; the new tests only reach `is missing`, `is not on PATH`, `not the launcher`, and `names the plugin folder`.

finding: Launcher bytes and the root round trip are tested only with the repo path; no test uses a plugin path holding a space or an apostrophe.
why: Windows user folders and plugin caches can hold spaces, and the sh form relies on shlex.quote while team_launcher_root re-parses it with shlex.split or a quote regex, so a quoting slip would make check and the permission test read a wrong or no folder.
fix: Parametrize the round-trip assertion with a root such as tmp_path / "a b" / "it's" for both launcher files.
evidence: `assert target.read_bytes() == data and pr.team_launcher_root(target) == PLUGIN_ROOT` (data comes from the same team_launchers call that wrote the file; only PLUGIN_ROOT is round-tripped).

finding: ENTRY_NAME shrank from `afk-team.py` to `afk-team`, so any allow entry that merely contains that text is reported `stale` instead of `missing`
why: An unrelated entry such as `Bash(git checkout 0027-afk-team-launcher)` makes the refusal say "replace it with `Bash(afk-team *)`", pointing the human at the wrong entry.
fix: Match stale on a Bash entry whose command word is `afk-team` or whose text names `scripts/afk-team.py`, not on the bare substring.
evidence: `stale += [(path, e) for e in entries if ENTRY_NAME in e and e != rule]` with `ENTRY_NAME = "afk-team"`
